categories.main_business_segments: Sunwels Co., Ltd. operates primarily in the nursing care business, with a single business segment focused on the operation of care facilities. Its main services include specialized nursing homes for Parkinson's disease patients (PD House), medical-specialized residential facilities, group homes for dementia patients, day-care services, home-visit nursing and care, care management, welfare equipment rental and sales, and the operation of a pressure training gym. The majority of revenue is generated from the operation of PD House facilities nationwide.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages specialized care protocols for Parkinson's disease, including high-frequency rehabilitation programs supervised by neurologists and university hospitals, and advanced medication management by nurses. It collaborates with academic institutions for ICT-based monitoring (using multi-sensors and wearables) to collect and analyze patient data, aiming to optimize care and rehabilitation. The company also develops proprietary training and certification programs (PD License) for staff to ensure high standards of specialized care.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers are elderly individuals requiring nursing care, with a particular focus on patients with Parkinson's disease and other intractable neurological disorders, as well as those with cancer, dementia, or severe disabilities. The company serves both private individuals and public insurance systems, with major revenue streams from national and local health insurance organizations. Its end markets are the rapidly aging Japanese population and the growing segment of patients with specialized care needs.
categories.geographic_coverage: Sunwels operates nationwide in Japan, with a concentration of facilities in major metropolitan areas (such as Tokyo, Osaka, and Fukuoka) and regional centers. As of the end of the fiscal year, it managed 43 PD House facilities and additional sites for other care services across Hokkaido, Kanto, Chubu, Hokuriku, Kansai, and Kyushu regions. There are no overseas operations at present, but the company has plans to expand online rehabilitation services internationally.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company is positioned at the downstream end of the healthcare and welfare supply chain, directly providing end-user services to patients and their families. It also acts as a service integrator, coordinating with medical institutions, insurance payers, and equipment suppliers to deliver comprehensive care solutions.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Sunwels is focused on expanding its PD House brand nationwide, enhancing its specialization in Parkinson's disease care, and differentiating through innovation in rehabilitation and ICT-based monitoring. R&D initiatives include joint research with universities on remote diagnostics, fall detection, and data-driven care optimization. The company is also strengthening compliance, internal controls, and staff training following recent regulatory and operational challenges.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through insurance reimbursements (nursing care, health, and disability insurance), direct user fees (for room, board, and non-insured services), and ancillary sales such as welfare equipment rental and sales. The company also receives income from public subsidies and, to a minor extent, from the operation of fitness gyms.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Sunwels is a leading player in the niche market of specialized nursing care for Parkinson's disease, with few direct competitors offering comparable nationwide scale or specialization. The company acknowledges the risk of new entrants imitating its business model but seeks to maintain barriers through proprietary know-how, academic partnerships, and brand strength. Its main competitors are general nursing care providers and emerging specialized care operators.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2025, Sunwels reported revenues of 26.5 billion yen, up 31.8% year-on-year, with a workforce of 3,302 employees. Despite rapid top-line growth, the company posted a net loss of 925 million yen due to one-off costs related to compliance issues and operational restructuring. The company has a high leverage ratio and is in a phase of aggressive facility expansion, aiming for long-term stable profitability after recent setbacks.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Sunwels differentiates itself through its focus on disease-specific care, particularly for Parkinson's disease, offering high-frequency, specialized rehabilitation and 24/7 medical support in collaboration with leading neurologists and hospitals. Its value proposition centers on providing high-quality, individualized care that addresses complex medical and daily living needs, supported by advanced staff training and ICT-enabled monitoring, resulting in higher patient satisfaction and improved outcomes.
